_note: Campaign flow, dialogue, memories and archive prose. IDs here are stable and referenced by save files.

missions.name: Signal Investigation
missions.summary: Investigate the anomalous signal and return with usable scientific data.
requirements: Propulsion that can lift the assembled ship
A scientific sensor with resolution quality 2 or better
Enough fuel and stored energy for the observation window

missions.name: Return With Evidence
missions.summary: This is not an unknown world. It is home, later. Return to the present with the archive records.
requirements: Recover the navigation chip from the Scrap King
Recover the power core from the Toxic Tide
Reach the Dawn Tower and its transmitter

memories.title: Green City
memories.frame: The projection is small and slightly out of focus. Bill holds it steady.
lines: Sunlight through leaves. A street with people on it.
A woman waves at someone just off the edge of the frame.
Bill: "I do not know whose memory this is. I only know I was asked to keep it."
Bill: "The coordinates are attached to the file. I cannot tell you why."

memories.title: Green City, Later
memories.frame: A second file, hidden behind the first. Bill hesitates before playing it.
lines: The same street, years later. The leaves are still green.
Someone has painted a mural over a wall of circuit boards.
Bill: "This is what the sorting crews were told they were protecting."
Bill: "They kept the picture on the wall. Nobody kept the instructions."
Nick: "Somebody believed it was worth keeping. That counts for something."

memories.title: Green Coast
memories.frame: Brine-stained film, projected at an angle. The sound is gone but the light is not.
lines: A working harbor. Water clear enough to see the bottom.
Fishing boats, gulls, a child holding a net far too big for them.
Bill: "The cleanup crews were shown this before every shift."
Bill: "It was labeled 'the target condition'. They were not told how to stop making the other one."
Nick: "Then we carry it out of here, at least."

memories.title: Dawn Forest
memories.frame: The projector hums. For a moment the dead trunks outside have leaves again.
lines: A forest so thick the light comes through in pieces.
Researchers in green jackets walk a boardwalk between the trunks, counting birds out loud.
Bill: "This is the Dawn Project survey, the year the tower was built. Every tree on this slope is in the archive."
Bill: "They built the shield to protect the records, not the forest. The forest was supposed to protect itself."
Nick: "Then the records are all that is left of it. We take them home."

entries.heading: SORTING LOG 4471
lines: Incoming tonnage: rising for the eleventh consecutive year.
Recovered material: falling. The discrepancy is logged under 'consumer turnover'.
A margin note in another hand reads: 'Please stop calling it turnover. It is waste.'

entries.heading: WARRANTY NOTICE
lines: Service bulletin: devices are to be replaced on the upgrade cycle, not on failure.
Repair depots are to be converted to retail floors.
The board approved the change unanimously.

entries.heading: IGNORED WARNINGS
lines: Groundwater survey: heavy metals above the recovery threshold.
Recommended action: relocate the sorting yards. Estimated cost: deferred.
Follow-up memo: the survey was accurate, the estimate was inconvenient, the item was tabled.
The item is still tabled.

entries.heading: SURFACE IMAGE 0012
lines: An orbital image. Blue ocean, pale cloud, a coastline that curves the way home does.
The image is old, but the shape is unmistakable.
Nick: "That's the coast. That's the shape of the coast where I trained."

entries.heading: MATCHING RECORDS
lines: The archive's place names match the ones in the VELA's flight computer.
The archive's dates do not.
Nick: "Every map is the same. Only the date is wrong. This is the same planet."
Nick: "This is home. Later."

entries.heading: CATCH REPORT
lines: Year 01: abundance. Year 04: abundance, with a note about size.
Year 09: the note is now the report.
Year 14: the report is a formality.

entries.heading: DISCHARGE PERMIT
lines: The facility was permitted to discharge into open water.
The permit was granted on the grounds that the ocean would dilute the output.
The permit did not measure what the ocean would keep.

entries.heading: SHORELINE SURVEY
lines: Sampling points 1 through 9: dead. Point 10: the facility's own outfall.
Recommended action: deploy an autonomous cleanup unit.
The recommendation was funded. The source of the discharge was not addressed.

entries.heading: CLEANUP UNIT LOG
lines: Unit designation T-9, marine cleanup and energy management.
The unit kept pumping after the water was gone.
Its classification routine was never updated: everything not seawater was contamination.
Including the people who came to shut it down.

entries.heading: HARBOR MEMORIAL
lines: A photograph of the working harbor, filed under 'target condition'.
Nick: "Bill showed me this. The boats, the gulls, the kid with the net."
Nick: "They had the picture the whole time. They just never changed the process."
Bill: "I can carry the picture. You can carry the proof."

dawn_archive.title: Dawn Project Archive
dawn_archive.subtitle: The final records, held behind the shield

entries.heading: PROJECT CHARTER
lines: The Dawn Project will record the living state of this region before it changes.
Every species, every stream, every season, for as long as the tower stands.
A note in the margin: 'So that someone, someday, can see what we were given.'

entries.heading: FOREST SURVEY 0001-0240
lines: Survey 0001: four hundred and twelve bird species counted on the north slope.
Survey 0120: two hundred and six. Logging permits approved for the lower valley.
Survey 0240: nine. The counting team requests reassignment. The request is granted.

entries.heading: SHIELD PROGRAM
lines: The archive shield was built to keep smog and debris away from the record vaults.
Its control interface accepts environmental archive terms as targeting signatures.
The engineers called it 'teaching the defense what it protects'. It worked until the smog learned to live inside it.

entries.heading: TRANSMITTER LOG
lines: The tower's transmitter repeats one packet: the archive index and a set of coordinates.
Destination field: 'anyone who can still change it'.
Nick: "That's the signal. The one I was sent to listen to. It was always addressed to us."

entries.heading: MAINTENANCE ASSIGNMENT B-4
lines: Unit B-4 assigned to carry the Dawn archive index and the green-city memory to the crash corridor.
Instruction: wait for a visitor who arrives from the signal. Show them what was lost. Help them leave.
Bill: "I did not know the last line was in there. I think I would have waited anyway."

briefing_intro: Mission control tracking. This is the briefing they gave us.
An anomalous signal has repeated for eleven days. Every model says it should not exist.
We take the VELA out, we listen, we record, and we come back with data.
briefing_requirements: Flight computer. Propulsion. Power. Comms. A sensor that can resolve the signal.
Enough fuel to hold the observation window, and enough stored energy for the instruments.
You have construction credits. Spend them on the ship, not on apologies.
briefing_outro: The console is beside the ship frame. Put VELA together, then run the preflight check.
If the check fails, revise the design. Nothing launches until it passes.
construction_intro: This is the assembly console. Every part earns its mass.
Preview a part before installing it. Previewing costs nothing.
preflight_pass: All checks green. The VELA is cleared for launch.
Nick: "Then let's go listen to the impossible thing."
preflight_fail: Preflight is holding the launch. Fix the design and try again.
launch: Liftoff. The sky goes from blue to thin to black.
The signal is stronger than the brief said. It is not coming from where it is supposed to.
rift: Nick: "Control, the starfield is wrong. Every star on the port side just moved."
The signal folds inward. The VELA is pulled sideways out of the flight path.
Debris hits the hull before the alarm finishes its first tone.
crash: No answer. The hull is holding. Most of the ship is not.
blueprint_memory: The wreck is the same ship you built. The surviving mass sits where you put it.
The flight computer is intact. That is something to work with.
junction_repair: The junction is dead. The wall is still warm, so something behind it still holds power.
Nick: "Hand me the scrap and I can bridge this."
Bill's chest lights up. The door answers.
bill_activation: Bill: "Power restored. Maintenance unit B-4 online. You may call me Bill."
Nick: "How long have you been sitting here?"
Bill: "A long time. You are the first thing that has asked."
Bill: "Before we do anything useful, there is something I was asked to show the next person who arrives."
Bill: "I would rather show you than explain it. My explanation is not good."
bill_idle: Bill: "The air is breathable. I am aware this is not reassuring."
Bill: "I do not know this sky either. We have that in common."
Bill: "I am told patience is a maintenance virtue. It is mostly what I have."
Bill: "Your manifest survived. I have been reading it. You built a careful ship."
crash_vela: The hull took the impact across the midsection. The frame is bent but readable.
Most of the science bay is gone. The flight computer is still inside.
Nick: "At least I know what I am looking at."
crash_polymer: Packed foam from the launch cradle. It saved the tanks, and it is worth carrying.
crash_rubble: A wall that used to carry signage. Whatever it said has rusted away.
The stone is warm. Not from the crash. From underneath.
city_intro: The route Bill gave us runs inland, through streets that were sorted into piles and left there.
Nick: "Circuit boards in the gutters. Whole pallets of them. Somebody stacked this on purpose."
Bill: "Sorting yards. They were told to recover everything. Then they were told to stop being paid."
Bill: "The control center ahead kept the records. That is where the coordinates were sent from."
city_memory: A maintenance shrine, still holding a charge after all this time.
Bill: "This one was left for whoever came next. I think that was always going to be you."
city_checkpoint: Nick: "Rest stop. I will mark the route so I can find it again."
Bill: "I will remember as well. Redundancy is a maintenance virtue."
city_boss_intro: The control center doors are welded shut from the inside. Something moves behind them.
A heavy chassis unfolds out of the dark, trailing magnets and stripped cable.
Bill: "Scrap King. It sorted waste for a living. Its control system no longer distinguishes waste from visitors."
Bill: "It throws what it cannot sort. Point the shield at the throw. Let the green motes through untouched."
Bill: "Absorbed motes charge your shield projector. When the meter above your head is full, press SPACE to send it back."
city_victory: The Scrap King folds down into its own sorting pile. The magnets cut out one by one.
Bill: "It is not dead. It is idle. There is a difference I would like to keep."
The control-center archive is drawing power again.
city_archive_done: Nick: "The place names match my charts. The coast, the ridge, all of it."
Nick: "The dates do not. Every one of them is wrong by the same amount."
Nick: "This is the same planet. This is Earth. Later."
Bill: "Then the mission changes. You are not here to listen to a signal."
Bill: "You are here to carry the record home."
Nick: "Then we go to the coast. The archive there still has power."
coast_intro: The coast road ends at a harbor that has not held water in a long time.
Nick: "The tide line is a stain, not a line."
Bill: "Marine cleanup facility ahead. Unit T-9 is still powered. Its classification routine is still wrong."
Bill: "Take samples if you want. The records will make the case better than we can."
coast_memory: A coastal projection, salt-stained and patient. Bill holds it steady.
Bill: "This was the target condition. I was asked to keep it where the cleanup crews could see it."
coast_checkpoint: Nick: "Marking the harbor route. If the facility resets itself, we start from here."
Bill: "The checkpoint is recorded. The facility's own logs are less reliable."
coast_boss_intro: Pumps engage along the outfall. The water is gone, but the machine is still treating it.
Toxic Tide unfolds from the pump housing: tanks, hoses, articulated arms, all of it corroded.
Bill: "It classifies everything as contamination. Including us."
Bill: "Different rhythm than the Scrap King. Shorter warning, wider spread. Keep rotating."
coast_victory: The pumps slow, then stop. Toxic Tide settles into the mud with a sound like a long exhale.
Bill: "The environmental archive is intact. The unit was treating the records as contamination too."
Nick: "Then let's take them somewhere they will be read."
coast_archive_done: Nick: "Catch reports, discharge permits, a survey with nine dead points out of ten."
Nick: "They had the picture of the harbor the whole time. They just never changed the process."
Bill: "The Dawn Tower is the transmitter that sent the signal. It is inland, past the ridge."
Bill: "With the navigation chip and the power core, the VELA's frame can be made to move again."
Nick: "Then we go back to the crash site and build it."
bill_phase_two: Bill: "I am carrying the archive. It is heavier than I expected."
Bill: "We are two components from a plan. That is more than we had at the crash site."
Bill: "Point the shield with the mouse. The machine does not need you to be brave, only accurate."
bill_phase_two_after_reveal: Bill: "You said the maps match. I have checked them eleven times. They match."
Bill: "I do not know what to do with that. I know what to carry."
Bill: "The coast archive is next. Then the tower."
base_return: The crash site looks smaller than it did. The VELA's frame is still bent, still readable.
Bill: "Navigation chip and power core. Two components recovered from two machines."
Bill: "Dawn Tower is unlocked on the chart. We can start assembling what the frame needs."
phase_two_complete: Bill: "And the record. Do not forget the record."
dawn_intro: Past the ridge the road climbs into what used to be a forest. The trunks are still standing. Nothing else is.
Nick: "No leaves. No birds. Just the trunks, like fence posts."
Bill: "The Dawn Tower is at the top. The project archive is inside, behind the shield the facility built to protect it."
Bill: "The shield emitter is the last component the VELA needs. Something is nesting around it. I can hear it from here."
dawn_memory: A survey projector, bolted to a boardwalk post. Its lens is clean. Someone kept cleaning it.
Bill: "This is the last memory in my index. I would like you to see it before we go up."
dawn_checkpoint: Nick: "Marking the boardwalk. If the tower throws me out, I start from here."
Bill: "Recorded. The vocabulary you learn up there will stay with you even if the fight does not."
dawn_terminal: A Dawn Project defense console, still warm. Its screen scrolls a word list: soil, habitat, conservation.
Bill: "The facility's defense interface reads environmental archive terms as control signatures."
Bill: "Type a term completely and the console fires a stabilizing pulse at whatever is in the shield."
Bill: "In plain words: the words are the keys. This is how the facility was built, not how real machines work."
dawn_boss_intro: The shield flickers open. Smog pours out of it and folds itself into wings, a skull of fused debris, two ember eyes.
Bill: "Sky Remnant. The smog that settled over this forest, living inside the shield it was supposed to be kept out by."
Bill: "It is shedding archive terms as it moves. The defense console will accept every one of them."
Nick: "Then I read them back to it. One word at a time."
typing_tutorial: Bill: "Quick briefing. Type the first letter of a falling word to select it."
Bill: "Finish the whole word to fire a pulse. No need to press Enter."
Bill: "A wrong letter restarts that word from its first letter. It does not hurt you."
Bill: "A word that reaches the red line hits you. Missed words come back later, so nothing is lost for good."
Bill: "ESC pauses the fight and opens the vocabulary journal. Reading is always safe."
dawn_victory: The last pulse lands. The wings come apart into ordinary haze and drift down the slope, thinning as they go.
Bill: "The shield is clear. The emitter is intact. That is the third component."
Bill: "Waking up. It has been waiting longer than I have."
dawn_archive_done: Nick: "Four hundred species, then nine. And a transmitter that kept calling for help."
Bill: "The record is complete. Navigation chip, power core, shield emitter. The VELA can be rebuilt."
Nick: "Then we go back to the crash site and build something that can carry all of this home."
workshop_intro: Bill: "The full workshop is online. Every part we fit is salvage, and the fabricator can only shape so much."
Bill: "Choose an engine, a route, protection, storage and what we carry. Then run the simulation."
Bill: "Simulating costs nothing. Fabricating spends salvage once. If a report fails, change the design and run it again."
Nick: "No credits this time. Just what we found and what we can make."
workshop_ready: Bill: "Fabrication complete. The VELA is assembled and the return mission checks out."
Nick: "Then all that is left is to fly it."
Bill: "Ready for final assembly. I will be in the seat behind you."

checkpoint.title: Phase 1 Complete
body: Bill holds the coordinates steady: a city, further inland than the crash site.
The VELA will not fly again, but the manifest survived.
The route to the Forgotten City is open.
